sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Around the world, parents, schools, and religious leaders talk about the importance of empathy.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，家长、学校和宗教领袖都在谈论同理心的重要性。

sentences.en: We tell our children that seeing things from another child's point of view is a sign of wisdom.
sentences.zh: 我们告诉孩子，能从他人的角度看问题是一种智慧的体现。

sentences.en: Today, we bring you two stories of empathy.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将为您讲述两个关于同理心的故事。

sentences.en: What makes these stories unusual is that this is not the ordinary kind of empathy we display toward friends.
sentences.zh: 这些故事的不同寻常之处在于，它们并非我们对朋友表现出的那种普通同理心。
这种同理心要困难得多。

sentences.en: It's about putting yourself in the shoes of your enemies.
sentences.zh: 它关乎设身处地去理解你的敌人。

sentences.en: I think that the two big elements that are lacking from the discourse on both sides is,
sentences.zh: 我认为双方在讨论中缺失的两个重要因素是：

sentences.en: one, a massive lack of hope, and two, this unbelievable lack of empathy.
sentences.zh: 第一，极度缺乏希望；第二，令人难以置信地缺乏同理心。

sentences.en: There's a reason we don't see a lot of this kind of empathy in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个世界上很少见到这种同理心是有原因的。

sentences.en: But also, one of the most enduring psychological drives in human nature is to be part of a tribe.
sentences.zh: 但同时，人性中最持久的心理驱动力之一就是渴望归属于某个群体。

sentences.en: When someone in our tribe starts seeing things from the point of view of another tribe,
sentences.zh: 当群体中的某个人开始从另一个群体的角度看问题时，

sentences.en: we have a name for people like that.
sentences.zh: 我们对这样的人有一个称呼。

sentences.en: What was most hurtful for me, most painful, was nobody stood by me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最伤人、最痛苦的是没有人站在我这边。

sentences.en: Hard though it is, this kind of empathy accomplishes remarkable things.
sentences.zh: 尽管很难，但这种同理心能成就非凡之事。

sentences.en: For one thing, when an enemy sees things from your point of view, she stops being your enemy.
sentences.zh: 首先，当敌人从你的角度看问题时，她就不再是你的敌人了。

sentences.en: This kind of empathy can melt hearts, bring down walls.
sentences.zh: 这种同理心可以融化坚冰，推倒高墙。

sentences.en: And that's what makes it dangerous.
sentences.zh: 而这正是它危险的地方。

sentences.en: And I'm staring at this wall out the window of the bus at the Kalandia checkpoint.
sentences.zh: 我盯着卡兰迪亚检查站公交车窗外的那堵墙。

sentences.en: And six million ghosts chase me as we drive through.
sentences.zh: 当我们开车穿过时，六百万个幽灵在追赶着我。

sentences.en: And I wonder if they will ever reSt.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是否能得到安息。

sentences.en: So my name is Avner Gwaryahu.
sentences.zh: 我叫阿夫纳·格瓦里亚胡。
我今年31岁，正好是今天生日。

sentences.en: Growing up, Avner Gwaryahu was a model Israeli patriot.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，阿夫纳·格瓦里亚胡曾是一位模范以色列爱国者。

sentences.en: I grew up in a religious family, what we call religious nationalist family.
sentences.zh: 我在一个宗教家庭长大，也就是我们所说的宗教民族主义家庭。

sentences.en: And I went to a religious high school, what we call in Hebrew a yeshiva.
sentences.zh: 我上的是宗教高中，也就是希伯来语中所说的“叶史瓦”。

sentences.en: I joined the army when I was 19 after doing a year of community service.
sentences.zh: 在做了一年社区服务后，我19岁参了军。

sentences.en: And I served for three years as a paratrooper in a special ops unit.
sentences.zh: 我作为特种部队的伞兵服役了三年。

sentences.en: But being a soldier came naturally to Avner.
sentences.zh: 但对阿夫纳来说，成为一名士兵是顺理成章的事。

sentences.en: In my society, in my community, in my family as well, you know, this was something that was discussed often.
sentences.zh: 在我的社会、我的社区，当然还有我的家庭里，你知道，这经常被讨论。

sentences.en: I'm named after a soldier who was killed in 1973 in the Yom Kippur War.
sentences.zh: 我的名字是为了纪念一位在1973年赎罪日战争中牺牲的士兵。

sentences.en: My dad himself was a paratrooper.
sentences.zh: 我父亲本人也是一名伞兵。

sentences.en: My older brother was a combat soldier.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥是一名战斗士兵。

sentences.en: The people around me, my mentors, my teachers, my counselors in my youth movement were all, of course, in the military.
sentences.zh: 我周围的人，我的导师、老师、青年运动的辅导员，当然都在军队服役过。

sentences.en: So I was really waiting for my chance to go and protect my country and serve.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在等待机会去保卫我的国家，去服役。

sentences.en: That was sort of something that I always knew I would do.
sentences.zh: 那是我一直以来就知道自己会做的事情。

sentences.en: And I wanted to be, you know, the best I could be at that.
sentences.zh: 而且我想，你知道，尽我所能做到最好。

sentences.en: But early in his military service, Avner started to see things that challenged his worldview.
sentences.zh: 但在服役初期，阿夫纳开始看到一些挑战他世界观的事情。

sentences.en: He was often asked to pull a maneuver known as a straw widow.
sentences.zh: 他经常被要求执行一种被称为“稻草寡妇”的战术。

sentences.en: This involved entering a Palestinian home to use the windows on the upper floors to cover other Israeli soldiers carrying out operations on the street.
sentences.zh: 这涉及进入巴勒斯坦人的家中，利用高层的窗户为在街上执行任务的其他以色列士兵提供掩护。

sentences.en: So I found myself in numerous cases throughout my service invading people's homes in the middle of the night most of the time after we knew that the people inside these homes were innocent because you do not want to enter someone's house if you know that he's involved in some terrorist organization.
sentences.zh: 在服役期间，我多次在半夜闯入人们的家中，大多数时候我们知道屋里的人是无辜的，因为如果你知道某人参与了恐怖组织，你是不想进入他家的。

sentences.en: So what we actually did is you find a house on a map, you choose the house because it's situated in the right place, because it's elevated enough,
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际做的是，你在地图上找一栋房子，选择它是因为它位置合适，因为它足够高，

sentences.en: because it has the right size windows.
sentences.zh: 因为它有大小合适的窗户。

sentences.en: And you enter this house, and you enter this house in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 然后你进入这栋房子，而且是在半夜进入。

sentences.en: Now, this house, from that moment on, belongs to the soldiers, right?
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，这栋房子就属于士兵了，对吧？

sentences.en: If the family wants to use the bathroom or the kitchen, in many cases, they need permission from the soldiers.
sentences.zh: 如果家人想用洗手间或厨房，在很多情况下，他们需要得到士兵的许可。

sentences.en: Of course, the family can't leave their house.
sentences.zh: 当然，家人不能离开自己的家。

sentences.en: And this dynamic between soldiers and Palestinians was something that I was part of for many, many nights.
sentences.zh: 这种士兵与巴勒斯坦人之间的动态关系，是我许多个夜晚亲身经历的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think that that's where I really learned, for the first time, first of all, a little bit about the Palestinians,
sentences.zh: 我认为那是我第一次真正了解了一些关于巴勒斯坦人的情况，

sentences.en: because I was never in a Palestinian home before I started my service.
sentences.zh: 因为在服役之前，我从未进入过巴勒斯坦人的家中。

sentences.en: I had no real contacts with Palestinians before I started my service.
sentences.zh: 在服役前，我与巴勒斯坦人没有任何真正的接触。

sentences.en: But also, I learned about the power dynamic that I was part of.
sentences.zh: 但我也了解到了我所处的权力动态。

sentences.en: Just the fact that I was born sort of in the right side of the green line, just the fact that I was born to an Israeli Jewish family, gave me the power.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我出生在绿线的正确一侧，仅仅因为我出生在一个以色列犹太家庭，就赋予了我这种权力。

sentences.en: To walk in with a helmet, with a gun, with my uniform, and I was in control of an entire family.
sentences.zh: 戴着头盔、拿着枪、穿着制服走进去，我就控制了整个家庭。

sentences.en: One night in particular stands out in his memory.
sentences.zh: 有一个夜晚在他的记忆中尤为深刻。

sentences.en: We were supposed to take over a house, and we were walking through sort of the open space around the house.
sentences.zh: 我们本应接管一栋房子，我们正走在房子周围的空地上。

sentences.en: We made maybe too much noise, or maybe we stepped on a branch, and we started hearing screaming from inside the Palestinian home.
sentences.zh: 我们可能制造了太大的噪音，或者踩到了树枝，我们开始听到巴勒斯坦人家里传出的尖叫声。

sentences.en: So me and the officer who were leading our soldiers went up to the window where we hear the screams because, you know, we could be detected, and that's not something we want.
sentences.zh: 于是我和带领士兵的军官走到我们听到尖叫声的窗户前，因为你知道，我们可能会被发现，而那不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: And we break the glass of this house, and we peer in with our rifles.
sentences.zh: 我们打碎了房子的玻璃，用步枪向内窥视。

sentences.en: We had flashlights on the barrels.
sentences.zh: 我们的枪管上装有手电筒。

sentences.en: And we see on the floor of this house an older lady, an elderly lady, helpless.
sentences.zh: 我们看到房子的地板上有一位年长的女士，一位无助的老妇人。

sentences.en: And she was on the floor.
I don't know what exactly happened, but maybe she heard us, and she was petrified, and she just fell off her bed.
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体发生了什么，但也许她听到了我们的声音，她被吓坏了，就从床上掉了下来。

sentences.en: I remember looking to the other side of the room, and I could see at the end of the corridor some people or voices, and it was her family who were petrified to come and help her.
sentences.zh: 我记得看向房间的另一边，我能看到走廊尽头有一些人或声音，那是她的家人，他们被吓得不敢过来帮她。

sentences.en: And I remember standing there and telling myself, this is not what I thought I would be doing.
sentences.zh: 我记得站在那里告诉自己，这不是我以为我会做的事情。

sentences.en: This is definitely not promoting the security of my country or the security of my family.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是在促进我国或我家人的安全。

sentences.en: And I started thinking, what about the family of this old lady?
sentences.zh: 我开始想，这位老妇人的家人呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what do they think about me now?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们现在怎么看我？

sentences.en: Moments like this are what prompted Avner to start working with an organization called Breaking the Silence,
sentences.zh: 正是这样的时刻促使阿夫纳开始与一个名为“打破沉默”的组织合作，

sentences.en: a group of military veterans who want to talk openly about what they've learned.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由退伍军人组成的团体，他们希望公开谈论自己的所见所闻。

sentences.en: From Avner's perspective, there is nothing unpatriotic about Israeli veterans telling their stories,
sentences.zh: 在阿夫纳看来，以色列退伍军人讲述他们的故事并没有什么不爱国的，

sentences.en: talking about moments they struggle with or Palestinian families they got to know.
sentences.zh: 谈论他们挣扎的时刻或他们所认识的巴勒斯坦家庭也一样。
但其他人有不同的看法。

sentences.en: In one recent video, a group targeting Avner shows a Palestinian attacking an Israeli with a knife.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一段视频中，一个针对阿夫纳的团体展示了一名巴勒斯坦人用刀袭击以色列人的画面。

sentences.en: The video then accuses four human rights activists, including Avner, of protecting the terroriSt.
sentences.zh: 视频随后指责包括阿夫纳在内的四名人权活动人士保护恐怖分子。

sentences.en: They called all four of us foreign agents, or what they called it were shtulim, which basically means implanted,
sentences.zh: 他们称我们四个人为外国代理人，或者他们称之为“shtulim”，基本意思是“植入者”，

sentences.en: meaning my opinions, my thoughts, and the actions of myself and my friends are not things we actually think on our own,
sentences.zh: 意思是我的观点、我的想法以及我和朋友们的行动，并不是我们自己真正思考的结果，

sentences.en: but we're actually working for foreign government.
sentences.zh: 而是我们实际上在为外国政府工作。

sentences.en: To us, it sounded as if they're blaming us for being spies.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，听起来他们是在指责我们是间谍。

sentences.en: As I was listening to Avner, I couldn't stop thinking about a study I read many years ago.
sentences.zh: 当我在听阿夫纳讲述时，我不禁想起了我多年前读过的一项研究。

sentences.en: Psychologist Lee Ross ran an experiment at Stanford University.
sentences.zh: 心理学家李·罗斯在斯坦福大学进行了一项实验。

sentences.en: He brought in students from a pro-Israeli group and a pro-Arab group
sentences.zh: 他找来了亲以色列团体和亲阿拉伯团体的学生，

sentences.en: and had them watch television news clips about the Arab-Israeli conflict.
sentences.zh: 让他们观看关于阿以冲突的电视新闻片段。

sentences.en: He found the pro-Israeli students saw lots of anti-Israel references in the news clips,
sentences.zh: 他发现亲以色列的学生在新闻片段中看到了许多反以色列的暗示，

sentences.en: whereas the pro-Arab students saw lots of anti-Arab references while looking at the very same news clips.
sentences.zh: 而亲阿拉伯的学生在观看完全相同的新闻片段时，却看到了许多反阿拉伯的暗示。

sentences.en: When Arabs and Israelis think about their conflict, each group desperately wants observers to know that they have been wronged.
sentences.zh: 当阿拉伯人和以色列人思考他们的冲突时，每个群体都迫切希望观察者知道他们受到了冤屈。

sentences.en: To acknowledge the pain on the other side is to somehow limit this claim.
sentences.zh: 承认对方的痛苦在某种程度上就是限制了这种诉求。

sentences.en: That's why two groups can look at the same reality and see completely different things.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么两个群体可以看着同一个现实，却看到完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: His story reminded me of the study.
sentences.zh: 他的故事让我想起了那项研究。

sentences.en: As you're telling me the story, I'm realizing that one of the psychological implications of your work
sentences.zh: 当你给我讲这个故事时，我意识到你工作的一个心理学含义是，

sentences.en: is that really when you try and empathize with what the other side is going through,
sentences.zh: 当你试图同情对方所经历的事情时，

sentences.en: there is something about that action that drives your friends and comrades really angry.
sentences.zh: 这种行为本身会让你的朋友和战友感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: That the idea that one of you would empathize with the other side feels like betrayal.
sentences.zh: 你们中的某个人会同情对方的想法，感觉就像背叛。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that you're touching a point which is true and I think is extremely difficult.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为你触及了一个事实，而且我认为这极其困难。

sentences.en: You know, silence is not an Israeli disease, is not an Israeli epidemic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，沉默不是一种以色列疾病，不是一种以色列流行病。

sentences.en: There is no society, there is no community that does not live with this disease of silence.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个社会、没有哪个社区不生活在这种沉默的疾病中。

sentences.en: A big part of what Breaking the Silence is saying is, you know, the fact that we are talking about our actions,
sentences.zh: “打破沉默”组织所说的大部分内容是，你知道，我们谈论自己的行为，

sentences.en: of course it doesn't mean there's no responsibility on the Palestinian side.
sentences.zh: 当然并不意味着巴勒斯坦方面就没有责任。

sentences.en: But, you know, when I do think about what can create change and who has the power for change,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我思考什么能创造改变，谁有能力改变时，

sentences.en: I can't ignore the fact that in this specific point, we are the ones with the power.
sentences.zh: 我无法忽视这样一个事实：在这一点上，我们才是拥有权力的一方。

sentences.en: When we come back, a Palestinian professor tries to get his students to empathize with Israelis.
sentences.zh: 回来后，一位巴勒斯坦教授试图让他的学生同情以色列人。

sentences.en: If you learn about the suffering of the other, would that help in your attitude for reconciliation?
sentences.zh: 如果你了解对方的苦难，这会有助于你对和解的态度吗？

sentences.en: The psychologist Michael Wall and Naila Branscombe once asked Jewish volunteers to think about the suffering of Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 心理学家迈克尔·沃尔和奈拉·布兰斯科姆曾要求犹太志愿者思考巴勒斯坦人的苦难。

sentences.en: The psychologist reminded some of the volunteers about the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 心理学家提醒一些志愿者关于大屠杀的事情。

sentences.en: Compared to others, Jews reminded of their own group's suffering showed less compassion toward Palestinian suffering.
sentences.zh: 与其他被提醒自己群体苦难的人相比，犹太人对巴勒斯坦人的苦难表现出的同情心更少。

sentences.en: The same thing happens with other groups.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情也发生在其他群体身上。

sentences.en: Americans reminded of traumas, even distant traumas like the Pearl Harbor attack,
sentences.zh: 美国人被提醒创伤，甚至是像珍珠港事件这样遥远的创伤时，

sentences.en: show less empathy for victims of torture carried out by American service members.
sentences.zh: 对美国军人实施酷刑的受害者表现出的同情心也较少。

sentences.en: In 1948, hundreds of thousands of Palestinians lost their homes during the creation of the State of Israel.
sentences.zh: 1948年，成千上万的巴勒斯坦人在以色列建国期间失去了家园。

sentences.en: Palestinians have a word to describe this trauma.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦人用一个词来描述这种创伤。

sentences.en: They call it the Nakba, the catastrophe.
Just as traumatized Israelis don't want to think about the Nakba,
sentences.zh: 正如受过创伤的以色列人不想去想“Nakba”一样，

sentences.en: traumatized Palestinians don't want to think about the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 受过创伤的巴勒斯坦人也不想去想大屠杀。

sentences.en: Muhammad Dajani used to be one of those Palestinians who struggled to empathize with Israelis.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德·达贾尼曾是那些难以同情以色列人的巴勒斯坦人之一。
他认为自己是一名民族主义者。

sentences.en: In fact, as a result of his political work for Palestinian statehood,
sentences.zh: 事实上，由于他为巴勒斯坦建国所做的政治工作，

sentences.en: Muhammad says he was forced into exile from his native Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德说他被迫流亡，离开了他的故乡耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: He was allowed to return in 1993 because his father was very sick.
sentences.zh: 1993年，因为父亲病重，他获准返回。

sentences.en: And then, just like Avner, something happened to Muhammad that shook his beliefs about his enemy.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像阿夫纳一样，穆罕默德身上发生了一件事，动摇了他对敌人的看法。

sentences.en: In the beginning, it was very difficult for me to adjuSt.
But my father, who had cancer, started taking me to Ayn Karim Hospital,
sentences.zh: 但我患有癌症的父亲开始带我去艾因卡里姆医院，

sentences.en: where he used to have chemotherapy.
And it made me observe my enemy, the Israelis, the doctors, the nurses, the staff.
sentences.zh: 这让我观察我的敌人——以色列人、医生、护士、工作人员。

sentences.en: I noticed that their attitude to my father was not an attitude of an enemy to his enemy,
sentences.zh: 我注意到他们对待我父亲的态度不是敌人对待敌人的态度，

sentences.en: but rather a doctor to his patient.
sentences.zh: 而是医生对待病人的态度。

sentences.en: Another time, Muhammad's mother suffered a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，穆罕默德的母亲心脏病发作。

sentences.en: He was in a car with her.
sentences.zh: 他当时和她在一辆车里。

sentences.en: We were coming to the Ben-Gurion airport exit, and my brother decided to take that exit.
sentences.zh: 我们正要到达本古里安机场出口，我哥哥决定走那个出口。

sentences.en: Muhammad told his brother he was being foolish.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德告诉他哥哥这样做很愚蠢。

sentences.en: Israeli soldiers would stop them, harass them.
sentences.zh: 以色列士兵会拦住他们，骚扰他们。

sentences.en: Muhammad's brother said they had no choice.
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德的哥哥说他们别无选择。

sentences.en: He pulled up at a security gate.
sentences.zh: 他把车开到了安全门前。

sentences.en: When we came to the gates of the airport,
sentences.zh: 当我们来到机场大门时，

sentences.en: and my brother told them that we have a sick woman with us, and they saw her.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥告诉他们我们带着一位生病的妇女，他们看到了她。
